title: New York City: Lower Manhattan
intro: Discover the city from the harbor to the Brooklyn Bridge. Five stops in Lower Manhattan connect waterfront views, small green spaces, and the streets where New York's history comes into focus.
author: Audio Tour

chapters.title: The harbor at your feet
chapters.transcript:
Begin at the southern tip of Manhattan, where the city meets New York Harbor. From The Battery, the water offers a sense of the journeys that have shaped this island.

Look across the harbor and notice the movement of ferries against the distant skyline. For generations, people have arrived here carrying plans, questions, and hopes. Before turning toward the busy streets, take a moment to let the waterfront set the pace.

chapters.title: A small green with a long story
chapters.transcript:
At Bowling Green, a small patch of green sits among the buildings of Lower Manhattan. This is New York City's oldest public park, a reminder that gathering places can outlast the city around them.

Notice how the curve of the park changes your view of the surrounding streets. There is a different rhythm here: a pause between the harbor and Broadway. Imagine the many versions of New York that have passed this same small space.

chapters.title: A quiet corner on Broadway
chapters.transcript:
At Broadway and Wall Street, look up at Trinity Church's stone spire. The present church opened in 1846, long before the towers that now frame it. Its scale tells a different story from the skyline around it.

From the sidewalk, notice the contrast between the churchyard and the movement of the surrounding streets. Stone, trees, glass, and traffic share this corner. The city does not replace every layer of its past; sometimes it builds around one.

chapters.title: A capital for a moment
chapters.transcript:
Outside Federal Hall, the statue of George Washington marks a site connected to his inauguration as the first president in 1789. New York was briefly the nation's capital. The columned building standing here today came later.

Look along Wall Street and consider the different kinds of power associated with this place: government, commerce, and the movement of money. A short stretch of pavement can hold several histories at once. Let the surrounding architecture bring those layers into view.

chapters.title: A bridge to another borough
chapters.transcript:
Our final stop is near the Manhattan pedestrian entrance to the Brooklyn Bridge. Opened in 1883, the bridge connects Manhattan and Brooklyn across the East River. Its stone towers and web of cables remain part of the city's familiar outline.

You do not need to cross the bridge to appreciate the idea behind it: separate places brought into conversation. Think back to the harbor where this tour began. New York is a city of connections, made visible in its ferries, streets, and bridges.
